title: Sinonasal Non-Keratinizing Squamous Cell Carcinoma Initially Misdiagnosed as a Benign Nasal Polyp: A Case Report
content: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is uncommon and can resemble benign inflammatory sinonasal disease, delaying diagnosis. We report a 59-year-old man with progressive unilateral rhinorrhea, recurrent epistaxis, and epiphora initially diagnosed as an inflammatory nasal polyp and treated without histopathological confirmation. Persistent symptoms led to endoscopy and biopsy confirming non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. CT revealed a soft-tissue mass in the left maxillary and ethmoid sinuses with frontal sinus extension and suspected adjacent skull-base involvement. The patient underwent surgical resection in April 2025, followed by 30 fractions of adjuvant radiotherapy; chemotherapy was recommended but declined. After treatment, symptoms resolved and serial CT examinations showed reduction of the lesion, although residual enhancing tissue remained indeterminate for fibrosis, inflammation, or viable tumor. The patient remained clinically asymptomatic during follow-up through 2026. This case supports early histopathological assessment of persistent unilateral sinonasal lesions and ongoing multidisciplinary radiological surveillance.
